script:
// touch-aggregator research workflow — adapted from
// .claude/skills/execute-research/templates/research.workflow.js
// Researchers run BLIND (no driver context) so their evidence is independent;
// the synthesizer reconciles them against context/driver-context.md.
export const meta = {
  name: 'touch-aggregator-research',
  description: 'Research how to build Touch (aggregator + touch-visual) over Claude Code session data and synthesize one complete implementation plan',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Research', detail: '6 read-only researchers, one perspective each', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'dedup + decide + write ONE complete plan', model: 'fable' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/home/laniakea/Projects/touch'
const TASK = REPO + '/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator'
const FINDINGS = TASK + '/findings'
const PLAN_FILE = TASK + '/plan/touch-aggregator-plan.md'
const DRIVER_CONTEXT = TASK + '/context/driver-context.md'
const S = REPO + '/.claude/shared/monitoring/status.sh'

const statusCmd = (plan, stage, state, msg) =>
  `ORCH_STATE_DIR="${TASK}" bash "${S}" "${plan}" ${stage} ${state} "${msg}"`

// The subject: every source a researcher may read.
const SUBJECT = [
  REPO + '/README.md — the product spec (authoritative on intent)',
  REPO + '/CLAUDE.md — repo orientation',
  REPO + '/.claude/skills/execute-research/ and implement-plan/ (SKILL.md + templates/*.workflow.js) — the agent loops Touch must show and control',
  REPO + '/.claude/skills/m-orchestrator/SKILL.md',
  REPO + '/.claude/shared/monitoring/ (monitoring.md, monitor_server.py, decision_watcher.py, status.sh, monitor.html, tests/) — existing prior art',
  REPO + '/.claude/local-orchestrators/ — carried-over run history from an EARLIER project (omnigent); read as examples only',
  '~/.claude/ — REAL session data: projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl, projects/<slug>/<sessionId>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl + *.meta.json, .../subagents/workflows/<runId>/journal.jsonl, projects/<slug>/<sessionId>/workflows/<runId>.json, sessions/<pid>.json, history.jsonl, file-history/, todos/, settings.json',
  '/home/agent/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.220 — the Claude Code CLI binary (~275MB); `grep -a` with a timeout settles questions the files cannot',
].join('\n')

const RESEARCH_CONTEXT = `
TOUCH (the product to be built, per README.md): a web page for visualizing and
managing subagents in a Claude Code session. Two components, "aggregator" and
"touch-visual". The main page is a terminal-styled web view over a Claude Code
session and is the PRIMARY user interface (the user drives Claude Code from the
browser). A left sidebar lists such terminal sessions; clicking one opens that
terminal. A per-terminal page shows n8n-like UML diagrams/graphs of the run,
WITH controls to pause, restart, start and terminate agent loops. The "loops"
are the ones defined by the execute-research and implement-plan skills.

REPO STATE: no application source exists yet — only README.md, CLAUDE.md and
.claude/ (skills + a working zero-dependency monitoring module + carried-over
run history). You are researching how to build it, not reviewing existing code.

ENVIRONMENT: everything runs in a sandbox. Ports are unreachable from the host
until published; services must bind 0.0.0.0, not 127.0.0.1. Outbound network is
firewalled (default-deny, HTTP 403). The existing monitoring module is
deliberately zero-third-party-dependency (bash + Python 3 stdlib + browser) and
its tests are stdlib-only scripts run directly with python3.

YOU ARE RESEARCHING BLIND ON PURPOSE: no prior conclusions are being handed to
you. Verify everything against primary sources yourself and report what the
evidence supports, including where the product as specified cannot work.
`

const RESEARCH_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', required: ['findings', 'findings_file', 'summary'],
  properties: {
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object', required: ['id', 'file', 'severity', 'title'],
        properties: {
          id: { type: 'string' }, file: { type: 'string' }, line: { type: 'integer' },
          severity: { enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor', 'nit'] },
          title: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
    findings_file: { type: 'string' },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

// DETERMINISTIC perspective list — one read-only agent per entry.
const PERSPECTIVES = [
  {
    key: 'sessiondata',
    focus: `The PERSISTED SESSION DATA MODEL. Enumerate, from real files under ~/.claude, every record
type and field an aggregator could read from a session transcript and its siblings: the JSONL envelope,
assistant/user messages, content block kinds, tool call + result shapes, usage/token accounting, mode and
permission records, titles, file-history records, system records. Establish what is written WHEN (flush
timing, batching, intra-turn visibility), what is redacted or spilled out-of-band, and what happens to
the files on /clear, /compact, resume and session end. Decide what a faithful "terminal view" can and
cannot be reconstructed from. Quantify latency empirically where you can.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'agentgraph',
    focus: `SUBAGENT + WORKFLOW GRAPH RECONSTRUCTION. Determine exactly how a run's node/edge graph can be
rebuilt from disk: subagent transcripts and their metadata sidecars, parent/child edges, spawn depth,
workflow journals, workflow run metadata, and any per-agent progress records. Distinguish sharply between
data the harness writes unconditionally and data that exists only because an orchestrator embedded a
convention in its prompts. Cover agent identity/naming, liveness (running vs finished vs abandoned),
ordering and timing when records lack timestamps, per-agent token/tool rollups, and how nested or
concurrent agents are represented. Say what an n8n-style graph of a run can honestly show at each moment
of its lifecycle.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'liveio',
    focus: `THE LIVE PATH: how a browser could show what is happening RIGHT NOW. Investigate every push or
low-latency channel a Claude Code installation offers — the hook system (enumerate the events and their
payloads, note which are synchronous/blocking), the running-session registry, notification and status
mechanisms, and any streaming output modes of the CLI. Determine whether raw terminal/PTY output exists
anywhere, and what it would take to obtain a real terminal stream. Judge freshness, ordering and failure
modes of each channel, and the cost each imposes on the user's actual session.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'control',
    focus: `THE CONTROL PLANE: can an external web page start, pause, restart or terminate agent loops?
Establish first what a "loop" IS at runtime by reading the skill templates (who spawns whom, where state
lives, what a resumable boundary is). Then find every mechanism by which anything outside a running CLI
process can affect it: process-level signals, sockets or IPC, CLI flags and headless/streaming modes,
job/background mechanisms, file-based channels, and any in-process control functions that exist but lack
a transport. For each of start/pause/restart/terminate, state what is actually achievable, what it does
to in-flight work and on-disk state, and what is semantically impossible.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'priorart',
    focus: `THE EXISTING MONITORING MODULE as prior art: .claude/shared/monitoring/ plus the three skills.
Read the implementation, not just the docs. Establish precisely which problems it has already solved
correctly (tailing semantics, checkpointing, replay, id rotation, token dedup, path containment, the
event schema and its reserved names, test approach), which of its assumptions break for Touch's broader
scope, and where it is structurally unable to grow (transport direction, coupling to the marker
convention, single-run assumptions, security posture). Recommend concretely what to reuse verbatim, what
to generalize, and what to replace — with the migration consequence of each.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'stack',
    focus: `IMPLEMENTATION STACK AND DELIVERY for aggregator + touch-visual. Decide the runtime, transport,
terminal-emulation and graph-rendering approach, weighing the repo's zero-third-party-dependency precedent
and stdlib-only tests against the sandbox's firewall and port-publishing constraints (verify what package
installs actually succeed here rather than assuming). Cover: process model and how the web tier reaches
session data; live update transport; how a terminal is rendered in a browser; how an n8n-style graph is
laid out and updated incrementally; state/reconnect semantics; auth and exposure of a local daemon that
can read credentials-adjacent files; testability; and repo layout consistent with CLAUDE.md.`,
  },
]

const researchPrompt = (p) => `
[monitor] plan=research stage=${p.key} role=research attempt=1
You are a READ-ONLY researcher on the subject below. Never edit any source file —
you only read, run safe inspection commands, and write ONE findings file in the
task state folder.
FIRST run: ${statusCmd('research', p.key, 'running', 'scanning ' + p.key + ' perspective')}

Subject (read all that your focus touches; line numbers matter):
${SUBJECT}

RESEARCH_CONTEXT: ${RESEARCH_CONTEXT}

YOUR PERSPECTIVE: ${p.focus}

Method: study the subject with adversarial/analytical intent; where cheap, verify
a suspicion empirically ONLY in a throwaway dir under /tmp/claude-1000 — never
against the live task folder ${TASK} except the two mandated status.sh calls.
Reading ~/.claude and grepping the CLI binary (use timeouts; it is ~275MB) is in
scope and encouraged; treat what you observe as the ground truth over any
documentation. Report only real, actionable items (defects, risks, gaps,
decisions to make) with a concrete rationale each.
Severity: blocker | major | minor | nit.

Write your FULL findings to ${FINDINGS}/research-${p.key}-attempt-1.md — one
section per finding: id ${p.key.toUpperCase()}-<n>, file:line (or the exact
command/path that proves it), severity, the concrete scenario, and a concrete
recommendation. This file is task state — writing it is required.
LAST run: ${statusCmd('research', p.key, 'done', 'found N findings')} (replace N)
Return structured output only: findings (id/file/line/severity/title each), findings_file, summary.
`

const SYNTH_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', required: ['plan_file', 'item_count', 'summary'],
  properties: {
    plan_file: { type: 'string' },
    item_count: { type: 'integer' },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

const synthPrompt = (reports) => `
[monitor] plan=synthesis stage=synthesize role=synth attempt=1
You are the PLAN SYNTHESIZER. READ-ONLY for source; you write exactly one plan
file in task state.
FIRST run: ${statusCmd('synthesis', 'synthesize', 'running', 'merging ' + reports.length + ' research reports plus driver context')}

Research reports (read ALL of them fully from disk first):
${reports.map(r => '- ' + r.findings_file + ' — ' + r.summary).join('\n')}

DRIVER CONTEXT (read this SECOND, in full — it is REQUIRED input):
${DRIVER_CONTEXT}
The research agents ran BLIND on purpose: they never saw that file, so their
findings are independent evidence. It carries the driver session's own verified
observations, two prior feasibility assessments, the product spec, the
environment constraints, and an explicit list of UNVERIFIED items. Where a
research finding and the driver context disagree, do NOT default to either —
open the primary source (~/.claude, the repo, or the CLI binary at
/home/agent/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.220) and decide; record the decision
and which side it overrode. Where they agree, treat the item as confirmed by
independent evidence and say so.

Subject:
${SUBJECT}

Tasks:
1. Merge + dedup the findings (same item from two perspectives = one, keep both
   ids as aliases). Discard non-items with a one-line justification each. Where
   two reports contradict, open the source and decide.
2. Decide every global/protocol question ONCE (canonical shapes, who tolerates
   what) so downstream work cannot diverge. At minimum decide: process ownership
   (does Touch host sessions or only observe them) and the consequence for every
   UI affordance; the canonical internal event/state model; the read pipeline
   (what is watched, how indexed, live vs historical); which of
   start/pause/restart/terminate ship first, by what mechanism, and what each
   honestly does to in-flight work; the technology stack justified against the
   sandbox firewall, the port-publishing constraint and the zero-dependency
   precedent; and the security posture of a daemon with read access to
   credentials-adjacent files.
3. Order the accepted items into ONE complete implementation plan. Per item:
   id, title, affected files (file:line), the finding ids it resolves, the
   decided approach, and what a test should cover. Do NOT partition the plan
   into sub-plans — implement-plan's divider owns divide-and-conquer; just keep
   each item concrete and self-contained enough to be partitioned later without
   re-research. Every item must name the files it creates or changes, since the
   divider partitions by file ownership.
4. Write the full plan to ${PLAN_FILE} (mkdir -p its dir first): the global
   decisions section, then the ordered item list. Findings stay in the research
   files — reference them by id + path. Include a short section listing anything
   that remains UNVERIFIED and the cheapest experiment that would settle it.

LAST run: ${statusCmd('synthesis', 'synthesize', 'done', 'plan ready: N items')}
Then:     ${statusCmd('synthesis', 'plan', 'done', 'plan written')}
Return structured output only: plan_file, item_count, summary.
`

phase('Research')
log(`spawning ${PERSPECTIVES.length} read-only research agents: ${PERSPECTIVES.map(p => p.key).join(', ')}`)
// Barrier is required: synthesis needs ALL reports to dedup across perspectives.
const reports = (await parallel(PERSPECTIVES.map(p => () =>
  agent(researchPrompt(p), {
    model: 'opus', effort: 'high',
    label: `research:${p.key}`, phase: 'Research', schema: RESEARCH_SCHEMA,
  })
))).filter(Boolean)
log(`research done: ${reports.length}/${PERSPECTIVES.length} returned, ${reports.reduce((n, r) => n + r.findings.length, 0)} raw findings`)

phase('Synthesize')
const synth = await agent(synthPrompt(reports), {
  model: 'fable', effort: 'xhigh',
  label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize', schema: SYNTH_SCHEMA,
})
if (!synth || !synth.plan_file || !synth.item_count) {
  throw new Error('synthesis produced no plan items — cannot hand off a plan')
}
log(`plan ready: ${synth.item_count} items in ${synth.plan_file}`)

return {
  raw_findings: reports.map(r => ({ file: r.findings_file, count: r.findings.length, summary: r.summary })),
  plan_file: synth.plan_file,
  item_count: synth.item_count,
  summary: synth.summary,
}

raw_findings.summary:
Researched the persisted session data model from real files under ~/.claude plus targeted `grep -a`/`dd` reads of the 275MB CLI binary (v2.1.220), and empirical probes in /tmp. 20 findings, 3 blockers.

WHAT EXISTS. The session JSONL is a mix of four record classes, and the CLI's own classification table (binary byte 259354279) is the ground truth: `transcript` (user/assistant/system/attachment), `boundary-cleared` (progress, file-history-*, last-prompt), `accumulate` (content-replacement, fork-context-ref, frame-link) and `last-wins` (mode, permission-mode, ai-title, custom-title, summary, tag, queue-operation, worktree-state, pr-link, bridge-session, …). Siblings: `<sid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` + `.meta.json`, `<sid>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/journal.jsonl`, `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, `~/.claude/file-history/<sid>/<hash>@vN`, `~/.claude/history.jsonl`, `~/.claude.json`. There is no `projects/<sid>/workflows/<runId>.json` — that path in the brief does not exist on disk.

THREE BLOCKERS.
1. `usage` is copied onto every split assistant record of one API response — 50 of 63 response groups span multiple records, so summing per record over-counts output tokens 2.09x (115,605 vs 55,396 deduped by `message.id`). `.claude/shared/monitoring/decision_watcher.py:154` already dedupes correctly; reuse it.
2. Thinking text is never persisted: all 44/44 thinking blocks in the main transcript, and every one in all 8 subagent transcripts, have `thinking: ""` with only a signature — despite `alwaysThinkingEnabled: true`. A transcript-sourced "thinking" pane is永 empty.
3. The transcript is not append-only. `performRemoveByUuid` truncates and rewrites the tail (the file shrinks); `performCompactTranscript` rewrites the whole file via `<file>.compact.tmp.<hex>` + rename, dropping everything before the compact boundary. Byte-offset tailing silently freezes.

LATENCY (measured, good news). The writer batches on a `FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS = 100` timer; a poll started inside a Bash call saw that call's own `tool_use` record land +0.10s later, before the tool finished. Intra-turn visibility is real and sub-second with zero instrumentation. The cost is torn tails: batches are one `appendFile` up to 100 MiB, and observed lines reach 46 KB — cut at the last `\n` and defer the remainder.

LIFECYCLE. `/clear` starts a NEW sessionId and new file under the same pid (CLI's own command description), so the sidebar must key on pid and re-resolve sessionId every poll. The transcript file is created lazily — a probe session produced `lastSessionId` in `~/.claude.json` but no `.jsonl` at all. There is no session-end record (a cleanly `/exit`-ed session just stops after `Goodbye!`). `sessions/<pid>.json` is not a heartbeat: it was 863s stale while the session was busy running six subagents, and is written with a non-atomic read-modify-writeFile. Liveness must be `/proc/<pid>` + `procStart` (verified = `/proc/pid/stat` field 22).

AGENT GRAPH. Async `Workflow` runs return only `status: "async_launched"` and never get a completion record in the parent transcript — the run graph exists solely in `journal.jsonl` (which has `started`/`result` entries with **no timestamps**, and a `result` that is a Python-repr string, not JSON). Workflow subagent `.meta.json` is a 63-byte stub with no description or toolUseId, so per-node labels can only come from the `[monitor] plan=… stage=… role=… attempt=…` marker in the agent's first user record.

TERMINAL VIEW VERDICT. Reconstructible: prompts (incl. slash/bash-mode forms), assistant text, every tool call with full input, every tool result with full untruncated output (richer than the TTY, which truncates), turn durations, usage, model/effort/skill attribution, the whole subagent tree, file diffs. Not reconstructible: reasoning, streaming deltas, ANSI, permission dialogs, status line, system prompt, intra-tool progress (`progress` records are in the schema but literally zero exist on disk), and session end. The binary contains a complete asciicast v2 recorder writing `<sid>-<ts>.cast`, but `CLAUDE_CODE_TERMINAL_RECORDING` produced no file in three probes (`-p` with `1`, `-p` with a path, and a real pty) and the literal appears only in env-schema tables — do not plan around it. The plan must explicitly choose: semantic re-render of the transcript, or Touch owns the PTY.

TWO CROSS-CUTTING RISKS. The CLI's retention sweep unlinks the transcript and `rm -rf`s the entire `<sessionId>/` subagent tree, so Touch must own its history rather than reading `~/.claude` as an archive. And transcripts plus `history.jsonl` hold unredacted file contents, command output and every prompt ever typed — with a 0.0.0.0 bind and a published port mandated by the sandbox, every transcript route needs a token.

Rebuilt the run graph from primary sources (live session dd469822…, workflow wf_829e6f58-b2f, and grep/dd reads of the 2.1.220 CLI binary) and found 17 actionable items, 2 blockers. The harness writes, unconditionally: per-agent transcripts with timestamps and message.usage; sidecars carrying agentType/description/toolUseId/spawnDepth/model (and parentAgentId only for depth-2+); a workflow journal of bare {type,key,agentId[,result]} lines; and, in the parent transcript, the Agent tool_use/tool_result pair and the single Workflow tool_result that names runId/transcriptDir/scriptPath. Everything else a graph wants is either convention or unavailable. Two blockers: (1) the label/phase passed to agent() are never persisted, so every workflow node on disk is an anonymous "workflow-subagent · opus · spawnDepth 1" — node naming is entirely the [monitor] prompt-marker convention; (2) the rich node record (index/label/phaseTitle/state/tokens/toolCalls/durationMs/attempt/resultPreview) lives only in memory and is flushed to <sessionId>/workflows/<runId>.json at exactly one call site, in the completion path, so it cannot drive a live graph. Majors: journal lines have no timestamps and journal order is not spawn order (proved — append order differs from transcript-first-timestamp order for the 6 parallel researchers); a 180s stall watchdog with up to 5 retries makes one logical node emit multiple "started" entries with new agentIds, which decision_watcher's stale-close guard provably never closes (phantom forever-running nodes); the journal key is a content hash so identical prompts collide and resumed runs replay agents with no journal entry at all; queued agents have zero disk footprint and the concurrency cap is min(16,max(2,cpus-2)), so the same fan-out renders smaller on a small host; transcript and snapshot paths key off the CURRENT session id, so /clear or /compact scatters one run across sibling dirs; toolUseResult.totalTokens is only the LAST API call's usage (measured 90,971 vs 1,235,241 summed — a 14x under-report) while totalDurationMs/toolStats/resolvedModel are trustworthy; there is no completion marker inside a transcript (measured healthy flush gaps up to 30s against a 180s harness stall threshold), so liveness must be three-state; spawnDepth is 1 for both direct and workflow subagents so it does not encode nesting; and workflow-agent user-retry/user-skip write nothing to disk, so a Touch-issued termination is indistinguishable from a crash unless Touch keeps its own control audit. The file ends with a per-lifecycle-stage table of exactly what an n8n-style graph may honestly assert at each moment, and the recommendation to render harness-derived structure and convention/declared structure as visually distinct layers — since the README's pause/terminate controls would otherwise sit on nodes the harness never confirmed.

20 findings on Touch's live path, all verified empirically against CLI 2.1.220, the running session (pid 622), and throwaway experiments in /tmp/claude-1000/liveio. Two blockers. (1) LIVEIO-1: there is NO way to attach to an already-running interactive Claude session — /proc/622/fd shows only /dev/pts/0, no unix socket exists until a background session is started, and daemon roster.json lists only daemon workers. Touch must OWN (spawn) every session it displays; README.md's "web view over claude code session" cannot mean mirroring the user's existing terminal. (2) LIVEIO-9: "pause" (README.md:6) does not exist anywhere in the CLI's control vocabulary — only interrupt, kill, stop_task and hook deny/block. Honest implementations are a blocking gate hook at SubagentStart/PreToolUse, or a cooperative control-file check inside the workflow script; both pause only at an agent boundary, which the UI must say. Restart is real and cheap: the Workflow runtime memoises agent() calls by prompt hash (journal key "v2:<sha256>"), so re-running with the same runId replays completed agents ("100% cache hit"). The big positive: I proved, twice, that a raw ANSI terminal stream with input, resize and kill is available locally — `<versioned-binary> --bg-pty-host <sock> <cols> <rows> -- <cmd> [args]` opens a unix socket with a 5-byte-header frame protocol (uint32BE len + uint8 kind; kind 0 = PTY bytes, kind 1 = JSON control), replays a 256KB scrollback ring then sends {"t":"live"}, and fans out to multiple subscribers. I drove a real interactive Claude REPL through it (36 frames, first at t+0.00s). Caveats: output is streamed to any connector unauthenticated (LIVEIO-3, and the input gate fails open when the tokens file is unreadable), and the interface is private/version-coupled (LIVEIO-4), so it needs a capability probe plus SDK stream-json as the declared fallback. For the graph page, hooks are decisive: all 31 hook events enumerated from the binary, every payload carries agent_id/agent_type, SubagentStart fires 70ms after spawn and SubagentStop hands over agent_transcript_path — but hooks are strictly blocking (measured: a sleep-3 PreToolUse hook added 3.10s to a 67ms tool; default timeout is 600s), so the hook must only append a line to a file. Transcript tailing is message-granular with 1-5s bursts and cannot back a terminal. The session registry has no heartbeat (622.json said status=busy with updatedAt 854s stale), so liveness must come from /proc+procStart or `claude agents --json`. Remote Control is an api.anthropic.com cloud relay and should be rejected.

A "loop" is a JS program running via vm.runInContext inside ONE claude process — verified by ps (PID 622 only) while six workflow agents ran concurrently — so no loop, agent or attempt has an OS identity to signal. For an already-running interactive session there is NO external control transport at all: claude listens on no TCP port, stdin is /dev/pts/0 with dev.tty.legacy_tiocsti=0 (injection disabled), no control.sock exists without the bg daemon, and no custom signal handler exists beyond terminate. The only supported channel is --input-format stream-json, whose control_request parser accepts exactly initialize/interrupt/set_model/set_permission_mode — verified live (interrupt returned success and killed the in-flight background task). Of the README's four verbs: START is fully achievable (three routes; structured control and terminal fidelity cannot come from one process). TERMINATE is achievable, cleanly via interrupt, destructively via process kill (which also loses the workflows/<runId>.json completion record, written only at run end). RESTART exists only as Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — same-session only, a model-facing tool call, resumable only at agent() boundaries, with in-flight agents respawned from scratch and no working-tree rollback. PAUSE as specified does not exist: the harness's own "pause" (kft) is the same function as kill (tve) with a different status string. The one genuinely new finding is that hooks are a working external control plane — a PreToolUse HTTP hook verifiably held a tool call 20s then released it, and its payload carries agent_id/agent_type, so Touch can pause, step and gate a single agent while siblings run; the limits are tool-boundary latency, a 600000ms timeout ceiling, and deny being visible to the model. Notably, per-agent kill/pause/skip/retry already exist in-process (ISd/Vfr/zfr) but are wired only to the Ink TUI with no transport out. 17 findings written to the findings file, including a five-item list of what is semantically impossible.

The existing monitoring module is a well-built read-only prototype whose craft should be mined and whose architecture cannot become Touch. Verified correct and worth reusing verbatim: torn-tail tailing with a truncation sentinel (monitor_server.py:330-356, decision_watcher.py:470-491), checkpoint-with-journal-identity plus atomic os.replace (:494-520), monotonic token deltas with message-id dedup (:154-197), /clear-/compact session-rotation path union (:86-100), realpath containment in safe_artifact_path (monitor_server.py:199-212), escape-first markdown + NODE_STATES whitelist discipline (monitor.html:299-321, 463-543), status.sh itself, and the query-string-as-state routing model.

Two blockers stop reuse-in-place. (1) The transport is one-directional by construction: handle() never parses the HTTP method or reads a request body, drain_client() exists purely to discard client frames, and unknown routes return the dashboard with 200 — there is nowhere to put a pause/start/terminate command or a terminal keystroke. (2) There is no authentication, Origin check, or Host check on a 0.0.0.0 bind; harmless for a read-only dashboard, but it makes the control plane CSRF-reachable from any browser tab the moment controls exist. Both must be designed before the first write endpoint.

Nine major scope breaks follow. The aggregation unit is a repo-local task folder, not a Claude Code session (~/.claude/sessions/*.json — sessionId/cwd/status/name/tempo/tmux — is never read, though it is exactly the sidebar model). Visibility is gated on the [monitor] prompt marker in one workflow journal, so ordinary session subagents (two exist in this session, with richer meta: agentType/description/toolUseId/spawnDepth) are invisible. Parallel fan-out is unrepresentable: the watcher builds labels from role+attempt and discards stage, so the six live researchers all read "research #1" and monitor.html:287 collapses them into ONE flow node — the exact case the n8n graph exists to show. The flat (plan, stage, state) schema has no node ids or edges and no version field, so it cannot be the graph source nor evolve over permanent history. agent_tokens() fully re-parses every running agent's whole transcript every second (measured 16 ms/2.26 MB at 6 min; ~300+ ms/tick extrapolated to a 2-hour run) on the thread that also tails the journal. Replay always starts at byte 0, one frame per event, with an untrimmed log DOM and a 500 ms full-resync option — measured ~1.5 MB/h of events, ≈3 MB/s per tab at an hour of history.

Control is where the prior art is structurally blind, and the CLI binary settles it: workflows are background tasks in a task registry, stopped with TaskStop({taskId}) and resumed with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — and the binary states stops "leave no transcript marker". So a paused run looks identical to a stalled one and the 60 s quiet debounce will fabricate a completion verdict for it; and a resume replays cached agent() calls into a NEW journal, which load_state() handles by resetting offset=0 and re-emitting the entire history into the same events.jsonl (duplicate rows and token deltas). The journal's per-spawn "key" content hash is the natural idempotency handle and is currently ignored. Finally, one watcher process watches exactly one run with all run identity in module globals, so N sessions x M runs needs a real ~800-line refactor into per-run objects plus a supervisor, not a wrapper.

Minor items: unknown ?task= silently streams a different task instead of 404; no method dispatch or 404 at all; multi-writer append safety rests on an undocumented one-write()-per-record invariant (proved: 0/800 corrupted with one write per record, 206/800 when a record spans two writes — so Touch must not carry terminal output over a shared append file); reserved magic names share the namespace with runtime-generated ids; classify() sleeps in the poll thread (~9 s stall on a 6-way fan-out); and the network layer has zero tests while the frontend is tested by grepping its own source — a posture that must be decided globally now (stdlib socket-level integration tests keep zero-dependency; a JS runner does not).

Stack/delivery research for Touch, verified empirically on this machine (probes in /tmp/claude-1000; nothing written to the live task folder except the two mandated status.sh calls and the findings file). 18 findings: 3 blockers, 9 major, 6 minor.

Two premises in the brief turned out to be false and change the design. (1) The firewall does NOT block package installs: `npm install @xterm/xterm dagre elkjs cytoscape mermaid` and a pip dry-run both succeeded through the CONNECT proxy. The real constraint is runtime offline-safety — the browser loading the page (especially from the host after `sbx ports --publish`) gets no proxy, so nothing may be fetched at page load. Rule to codify: stdlib-only at runtime, npm allowed only to vendor pinned, committed assets (note .gitignore:18-19 ignores node_modules/ and dist/, so vendored files must live at touch-visual/vendor/). (2) `node-pty` cannot build here — no g++ in the image (`make: g++: No such file or directory`), while Python's stdlib `pty` works end-to-end including TIOCSWINSZ resize, so the PTY tier must be Python.

Blockers. No local control channel exists on a running CLI: `messagingSocketPath` is emitted undefined in the 2.1.220 binary, no session sockets exist on disk, and `--remote-control` is an Anthropic cloud bridge (`/v1/sessions`, "will not appear in the Claude app"). Touch can only drive sessions it spawns itself; every other session is read-only transcript replay, and the sidebar must show the two classes differently. Spawning is booby-trapped: a `claude` launched from inside an agent session inherits `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1` and prints "Transcript saving is off" — verified live, and verified fixed by scrubbing CLAUDE*/AI_AGENT from the child env — which would silently starve the entire graph half of data. And the existing server binds 0.0.0.0 with no auth and never reads the Origin header: a probe handshake with `Origin: http://evil.example` got a 101, so adding keystroke input to that socket is cross-origin RCE against a session running --dangerously-skip-permissions with ~/.claude/.credentials.json readable.

Transport/terminal. The existing WS cannot receive: `parse_client_frames` deletes payloads without unmasking (monitor_server.py:307) and a masked client frame is silently dropped (verified). The 0.5s poll (monitor_server.py:378) is a latency floor no terminal survives; the verified alternative is `pty.openpty()` + `Popen(start_new_session=True)` + `loop.add_reader` inside asyncio (never `pty.fork()`). Captured bytes from a real claude TUI include alt-screen, mouse 1000/1002/1003/1006, bracketed paste, DA1 identification queries and 24-bit color, so xterm.js (489KB UMD + 7KB CSS) is required — hand-rolling means dropping the terminal-fidelity requirement. For the graph, do not vendor a layout engine (dagre.min 284KB, elk 1.6MB, cytoscape 435KB, mermaid 84MB installed): the loop DAG's ranks are fixed by the two workflow templates and monitor.html:296-318 already prototypes the flow strip — hand-roll layered SVG with stable node ids so updates patch rather than re-layout.

Control. Loop restart is an in-session `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})` tool call (binary strings, plus "completed agents return cached results") — there is no external API, so buttons must be queued, acknowledged intents gated on `status: idle` from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, with honest verb definitions. Terminate needs an escalation ladder: SIGTERM was verified to leave an interactive TUI running; SIGHUP/closing the master and SIGKILL work, EOT exits cleanly. A real local PTY-socket surface does exist for background agents (/tmp/cc-daemon-1000/<id>/{control.sock,pty/<id>.sock}, hard-coded 200x50) — documented as deliberately not used, since it is undocumented and version-coupled.

Also: key sessions on (pid, procStart) — procStart equals /proc/<pid>/stat field 22, verified — since sessionId rotates on /clear; the registry keeps ghosts for a passive reader while `claude agents --json` (0.65s, supported, TTY-free) prunes them; expose typed projected endpoints over ~/.claude rather than any path parameter; poll at 250ms (0.39ms per full scan, no stdlib inotify); one process on one port (default 8932, since 8931 is the live monitor); and put app source at repo root as aggregator/, touch-visual/, tests/ with a run_all.sh, keeping .gitignore edits additive so test_shell.py:155 keeps passing.

result.summary: Merged 6 research reports (110 findings) plus driver context into one plan: 6 conflict resolutions decided against primary sources (driver overridden on write latency and bg-pty-host invocability; confirmed on tool-results spill via binary re-grep), 14 binding global decisions (Touch hosts sessions rather than attaching; owned vs observed class split drives every affordance; touch-events-v2 single stream with ref-union keys in repo-local .touch/; (pid,procStart)/uuid/message.id/(runId,key,ordinal) identity; Python 3.11 stdlib asyncio one process on 8932 with vendored xterm.js and hand-rolled SVG graph; per-boot token + Origin allowlist + typed endpoints; honest control table — start/terminate deterministic v1, stop/restart model-mediated with observed confirmation, pause only as hook-gate at tool boundaries v1.5, suspend impossible), and 23 ordered implementation items each with files, resolved finding ids, approach, and test coverage, plus discarded-findings register and 10 UNVERIFIED items with cheapest settling experiments.
